blocks.text: You can configure the Zscaler service to capture traffic that matches policy criteria, content scan signatures, or any other detection logic for later analysis. Zscaler offers multiple ways to capture network traffic. With Zscaler Traffic Capture Essentials, you can capture traffic as PCAP files for supported actions with Internet & SaaS (ZIA) policies. Your organization must have an S3 bucket configured to store capture data for Traffic Capture Essentials. To learn more about Amazon S3, refer to the Amazon S3 documentation. Your Amazon S3 bucket configuration must have the appropriate permissions to ensure that capture files are uploaded and ingested properly. For an example, see page 23 of the Zscaler and Vectra Deployment Guide.

If your organization has Traffic Capture for Network Detection and Response (NDR), you can capture traffic as PCAPNG files with the Traffic Capture policy. To learn more, see About Traffic Capture Policy and Configuring Settings for the Traffic Capture Policy.
When configuring your S3 bucket, Zscaler recommends using dual-stack storage endpoints for all cloud destinations.

blocks.item: From the navigation menu, go to Internet Access > Traffic Capture > Settings.
On the Traffic Capture Essential tab, click Edit.
In the Edit drawer:
Click Enable Traffic Capture Essential to enable configuration for Traffic Capture Essentials.
In the AWS S3 Settings section:
AWS Access ID: Enter the ID associated with your organization's S3 bucket.
AWS Secret Key: Enter the password associated with your organization's S3 bucket.
S3 Folder URL: Enter the URL associated with your organization's S3 bucket.

The Zscaler service does not support custom or directory-style bucket URLs that include non-standard prefixes, additional subdomains (e.g., s3express), or unconventional naming patterns (such as double dashes). You must use a general purpose S3 bucket URL following the standard format: https://<bucket-name>.s3.<region>.amazonaws.com/<path>.
HTTP Header: (Optional) Enter a string to add metadata to the Amazon S3 REST request:
Key: The case-sensitive name of the HTTP header.
Value: The parameters for the HTTP header.
For example, you can use HTTP headers to include the information necessary for configuring server-side encryption with customer-provided keys (SSE-C).
After you have entered the information, click Test Connection to verify the status of the connection.
(Optional) in the Per Occurrence Limits section, set limits or use the defaults:
Storage Limit: The maximum amount of data to be kept in the file when a policy configured for Traffic Capture Essentials triggers.
Sampling: The percentage of traffic that is sampled for capturing when Traffic Capture Essentials is triggered.
(Optional) In the Obfuscate section, choose to obfuscate information in Traffic Capture Essentials data:
Usernames: Choose whether usernames in created PCAP files are Visible or Obfuscated.
Devices: Choose whether device information in created PCAP files is Visible or Obfuscated.
See image.
Click Save and activate the change.
For the following policies that allow Traffic Capture Essentials, you can enable the Capture option:
Advanced Threat Protection
File Type Control
Firewall Filtering
DNS Filtering
IPS Control
Malware Protection
URL Filtering
